name: walkthrough
title: Building an LR Parser from the Grammar Up
description: Construct the item NFA from a grammar, run the subset construction to get the LR(0) DFA, then trace reduces showing exposed state and GOTO lookups.

steps.description: Item NFA construction and subset construction code.
Grammar: four productions for S', S, and X.
ITEMS: every item is a production with a dot position.
Show: formats an item with dot in the right place.
Edges: builds NFA arrows, one for the symbol after the dot and epsilon arrows to productions of nonterminals.
NFA output: prints all 11 item states with their transitions.
Eps_closure: follows epsilon arrows until nothing new appears.
Move: collects all destinations on a given symbol.
Subset construction: builds DFA states as epsilon closures, each state is a set of NFA items.
DFA output: prints all 8 states with their item sets and transitions.

steps.question: How many NFA states does the grammar generate?

steps.description: Move to Block 2: the reduce trace showing exposed state and GOTO lookups.
LR(1) table driver that prints reduce details.
ACTION table: maps (state, token) to shift, reduce, or accept.
GOTO: maps (state, nonterminal) to the next state after a reduce.
Parse: the LR parser loop with shift and reduce cases, after each reduce it prints production, exposed state, and GOTO lookup.
Trace: runs parse on input xxyyx, prints the full trace with reduce details.

steps.question: What does the first reduce print for production 3 on input xxyyx?
steps.answer: production 3 is X -> y: pop 2, exposed state 3, GOTO[3, X] = 6
